prompt: CSS box-shadow spread distance corner radius adjustment proportion
answer:
When the border radius is smaller than the spread distance, CSS adjusts the spread for the shadow’s corner radii using:

\[
\text{adjustment proportion}=1+(r-1)^3
\]

where:

\[
r=\frac{\text{border radius}}{\text{spread distance}}
\]

The effective spread used for the corner-radius calculation is therefore:

\[
\text{effective spread}
=\text{spread distance}\times\left[1+(r-1)^3\right]
\]

This adjustment is intended to create sharper corners for small border radii and avoid discontinuous behavior at `border-radius: 0`. The cited discussion says this adjustment applies to positive spread values; negative-spread behavior was treated separately. ([W3C issue #1900](https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/1900), [W3C mailing-list discussion](https://lists.w3.org/Archives/Public/www-style/2014Apr/0111.html))
